notes.title: Keysight 1.4.0 beta 1 now available to test on beta branch!
notes.content:
Hello! It's been a hot minute since the last update to Keysight, but don't be misled in thinking development has slowed down. In fact, version 1.4 is taking a while because it's another large-scale overhaul to core systems in Keysight!

The beta branch now contains the first preview build of 1.4 for you to try. If interested, simply right click on Keysight in your library, navigate to Properties > Betas, and select "beta" from the dropdown.

[b]You may want to wipe your save data and start fresh, to take advantage of new default presets and configuration[/b]. This can be done by typing "reset" into the console command field under System, and will instantly yeet all your Appdata for Keysight and reboot into the setup wizard.

[b]Warning: the entire basic menu is offline pending a rework[/b], and only the main Core/Effects/Scene menus have been fully reworked at this time. It's going to take me another good few weeks to finish up all other menus, but I really can't keep all the exciting new features to myself anymore!

[h1]Changes[/h1]
I'll save my usual novella-length announcement for when this actually hits the live branch, but here's a quick overview of the key changes:

[h3]Pulses[/h3]
Pulses have been [i]completely[/i] reworked, on the scale of particles moving from version 1.2 to 1.3. Pulses now use 2-axis graphical editors for animations, have a nicely organised editing menu, can animate their position over time, and [b]use sprite sheets as stencils[/b]. GIF support!

[h3]Note object meshes[/h3]
All note object 3D meshes have been rebuilt for consistency in Z-height, width, and border proportions. In addition, the way note objects scale has been changed to be entirely "relative". So minimum-scale of 1.00 now gives the natural shape of that geometry style, and a height offset of 1.00 gives a note-depth's worth of vertical displacement

[h3]Menu[/h3]
This beta contains about 50% of a full menu rework, with Advanced Core/Effects/Scene menus featuring universal use of new slider and graphical editor UI elements. [b]Tooltips are everywhere now[/b], if you don't understand what an option does, try hovering over the slider title or any associated text for a quick explanation!

[h3]Default presets and particle templates[/h3]
I've been pretty obstinate with not investing a ton of time creating great default presets in the past. With three graphics presets, it ends up being a good amount of work to perfectly configure a theme 3 times... BUT. The observation that [i]most[/i] users do not touch default settings has convinced me that a bigger default preset line-up is important. So: [b]13 default presets up from 4![/b] And 13 particle templates up from 9. Preset configuration and randomizer behaviour in Low/Very low is also much improved over 1.3

[h3]Performance[/h3]
Speaking of particle templates, several older templates have been updated to perform better as part of a general optimisation pass! Identical presets from 1.3 to 1.4 should perform about the same, but new default presets and usage of certain particle templates perform upwards of 2x better. All Standard graphics preset default presets perform at a GPU cap of around 120-180fps at 1080p under shift+Q turbo note testing mode on my 2060 Super. On a 16" 2019 Macbook Pro (AMD 5500M), this drops to 30-45, but the Low presets are all 100+fps!

[h1]Full changelog[/h1]

[This preview does not contain reworks for the basic menu mode, the colour settings menu, or anything below Core/Effects/Scene. Use at your own risk]

--- OVERHAULS ---

Overhauled pulses! This is on the scale of the particle rework from 1.2 to 1.3, so it's difficult to summarise the changes. Quick feature list:
- Pulses can now use sprite sheets as stencils! These can be easily generated from GIFs, so, basically: GIF support is now a thing!
- All animations are now controlled using 2-axis blends, and are properly organised
- Pulses can move their Y-position over time; with careful tuning these can match notes travelling up or down to lock a pulse to a notes

Overhauled default presets and particle templates! We now have 12 default presets + 1 exposed "default" plain preset for each of the graphics presets, and 13 particle templates. It is highly recommended to either fully reset Keysight using the "reset" command in Advanced System > enter console command, or reload default presets by clicking the desired graphics preset in Graphics

Menu style has been updated! Sub-headings, buttons and text now are much more visually distinct, which should aid in legibility of larger menus with lots of sub-headings. Large menus have been split into further sub-tabs, such as in the case of Impact Lights which now have 4 sub-tabs to break up that giant wall of sliders, and these subtabs are kept at the top of the tab to reduce the amount of scrolling up and down switching between sections. Additionally, text and buttons are using much more robust inherited styling to achieve this, which allows for easy global tweaks to menu style down the line if need be, and easier tooltip-ing! Which, speaking of, every single item in the menu now has a tooltip explaining its function. In the case of sliders and graphs, hovering over the title for the UI element will give a general explanation for what that element controls

Overhauled the way the menu switches between basic and advanced modes. The menu should now cleanly transition to the correct submenu in the other menu style, making it pretty seamless to play around in Basic mode, decide "I need to look at advanced options for a second", and click the button to quickly have a look, and then transition back without having to re-open any menus. The only menu that does not transition cleanly is Basic Colour, as this has no unambiguous equivalent in Advanced mode.

Overhauled the graphical editor and slider UI modules! This is getting its own separate entry in the Overhauls section because holy heck it took a lot of painstaking work to update. In the graph editor: big bulky buttons have been replaced with simple icon buttons, the layout has been tightened and tidied, graph bounds editing now auto-greys-out when the buttons will not do anything, and "use flat value" no longer changes the graph values and just uses the graph 'max' effect value (so you can switch between flat/dynamic response much smoother). In the slider: changed appearance of icon buttons, and fixed the bounds to properly update when trying to map to a value that sits outside the default min/max range. Snapping has been reworked from percentage based to a set snap amount that gets larger as the range increases, and the bounds for sliders and graphs can be re-written with finer control by clicking on the display and typing a new desired value. Additionally, very large values with many zeroes switch to using K (and M), such as 10,000 > 10K (and text entry respects this, so you can type in 20k and it works)

Overhauled impact lights! Candle flickering now uses 2-axis graphs for flicker speed and brightness deviation, as well as having a new property of "displacement by note activity"! This allows impact lights to subtly (or not so subtly) move around as they flicker, giving that classic candlelight dancing-shadows look. Vertical axis displacement is now also a 2-axis response with velocity, which allows for converting static on-piano impact lights to floating orbs that shoot up and down the backdrop in response to velocity! (Make sure to enable affect-backdrop for this, and you may need to tweak simulation values to get a good animation feel since these affect how impact lights react to note-offs)

Overhauled menu layout and "expose" behaviour for particle systems! Particle system editing now has a hiercharchical tab view to avoid being yeeted into the void when you open a giant tab, scroll down, and then opening a smaller tab below it (closing the first one). Particle behaviour sub-tabs are roughly organised by "importance of influence", with more-important options towards the front of a scroll box of tabs. "Expose" flags are also present per-tab, and control the entire tab. This means a basic user might see more options than previously, but it is also much more consistent and universal in terms of which tabs are visible in what mode

Overhauled particle randomization! This ties into the "expose" rework listed above, but the randomizer now randomizes each section of particle systems based on the "expose" flag for that section (if it choses to do randomize at all, based on the chance branch to randomize template particle systems). Previous behaviour simply randomized a handful of known-important values like path stretching and particle size, but notably did not touch things like particle shape as it was conceivable that particle shape is core to the template's function, and it should not be changed (as in the instance of the Steam template). Randomization operates within ranges of the original template value, and clamps to the graph min/max for each variable. This means that the randomizer will now more thoroughly and intelligently generate cool particle system modifications, and do so based off human-set value bounds so it doesn't go too crazy. If making your own particle templates, this means it is extra important to set good graph ranges even for things that are not used, along with deciding which sections should be exposed and therefore randomizable, and which ones should not

Overhauled note object shapes and scaling behaviour! Note objects are now much more consistent between shape versions, with each shape always being the same Z-height of 0.5cm and having identical border widths for narrow/wide borders. Black notes are also slightly wider across the board. On top of this, the way note objects scale to their minimum scale size and width scaling has changed significantly. Minimum scale is now relative to the size of two end caps, so 1.00 minimum size always gives a square/round note profile if released quickly. Cap size also scales with width, so the note object proportion is consistent across different sizes. Note scale can also be a dynamic response against note strength, bring on the chonky notes! You better be confident in your voicing, though

Overhauled (*clears throat*) translucent material domain sort priorities. Layman's terms: the layering of rings and pulses! Before, this was left up to the engine, and this worked just fine under most normal circumstances, but completely fell apart and gave weird "slow Z-fighting" if you layered a ton of fully opaque semi-transparency-supporting objects like pulses. Now, the sorting priority is manually set based on the Z-height above backdrop of pulses and particles, along with the order that they were spawned. Sort order is descending and goes in order of pulses > particles, so higher pulse slots and particles render underneath lower pulse slots/particles, but *ascending* with time. This means at each height, each new object is guaranteed to render on top of the last. The only limitation is that the accuracy of Z-height is limited to 0.01 thanks to int16 sort priority storage space. This opens up really exciting preset opportunities relating to deliberately overlaying TONS of stuff and letting it all bleed together, as this no longer flickers like crazy!

--- SMALL ADDITIONS ---

Added brightness slider for white key material and backdrop self-lighting to the Basic Effects > Backdrop menu. These two sliders should vastly simplify the common desire to have an always-visible backdrop, or brighter white keys

Added local cull horizontal and cull vertical rendering options to pulses and particles. This means that allowing or disabling pulses and particles clipping outside the active area is now controlled per pulse/particle, although both have both culling options enabled by default. Psst, some particle systems look great when falling below the keyboard dividing line, like "sandstorm"!

Repurposed the Core > Viewport culling toggles for horizontal and vertical axes. These now exclusively act on the backdrop, and are found under Scene > Backdrop. Enabling "extend backdrop bounds horizontally/vertically" will turn the backdrop into more of a "canvas" for advanced, not-specifically-piano visualisations. (I mention the repurposing because if you had culling disabled prior to this update, it will essentially turn ON these new extend-bounds options)

Added tooltip fade-in delay slider to System > Interface. This allows you to set a longer or shorter time period that you need to hover over something for it to show the tooltip

Added support for transparent piano key materials. You probably still shouldn't use these, but it was simpler to allow them than to check and block transparent material pasting

Added rename functionality to pulse and particle slot titles (just click on the text and edit it), and removed the rename field from the pulse picker

Added "force release after set time" function to particles. This overrides their usual release-when-note-is-released behaviour, and causes them to release a set amount of time after they spawn. This can create "bursts" of particles with a short release time and a high spawn count. Note that dynamic velocity response is disabled for this mode

Added time offset functionality to particle systems using force-release-after-set-time mode. This functions the same way as pulses, but is rather more niche in its utility

Added debug functionality to arrow keys. Left arrow pauses and unpauses Keysight, up/down changes time-stepping, right arrow increments time by specific amount

Added ability for vsync interval to be set to 0. This activates rhi.SyncWithDWM 1, which theoretically syncs frames to the desktop window manager rather than the monitor, which may assist in recording software frame pacing. But it also seems to remove all frame limits, so, this requires more testing

Added ability to have greater than 1.0 normal map strength on Advanced materials, and added ability to have negative normal map strengths. Large values increase the perceived geometry distortion, negative values "flip" the Z-direction of distortion

Added texture panning over time to note objects, backdrop and overlay materials! This allows texture unwrapping to change over time, adding another layer of complexity to visuals if desired. Speed is measured in the same speed units as notes, or 1.0 = 10cm/s

Added "flip mask" option to materials, and removed "- (inverted)" default masks for advanced materials with an alpha mask, or blended materials

Added "geometry normal strength" slider to note object behaviour. This is a complex one to explain, perhaps, but: setting geometry normal strength to 0.00 causes all pixels from a note object to believe they are pointing "upwards", and then modified by the normal map from the material (if using one). Functionally, this allows you to control the amount of reflection warping given by the note geometry without actually changing the geometry itself, which is useful for making flat-looking notes with a specific outline shape without having that shape's reflection warping (so, round notes without round reflections)

Added a metric to the information tab of the particle system menu to display the approximate GPU cost of the current system. This is calculated fairly lazily by taking the max time, size, spawn rate and lowest speed and multiplying them together, as the primary cost for high-intensity systems like Steam is the translucent shader render cost on all the overlaid particles. Higher = worse, and typically anything over 100.00 enters frame-drop territory on weaker systems. Be aware that particle systems have plenty of other costs associated with them, not just pixel translucency cost, such as: CPU cost to pass in dynamic variables to the particle system, GPU cost to simulate particles, and GPU memory cost to store particle data

Added culling to midi events that violate basic midi rules. This is to account for midi files that give weird, illegal messages like midi channels of 226 (when it should be 0-15), or velocities of >127. Any incoming events with either channel outside range of 0-15 (or 1-16 when offset) / control ID outside of 0-127 / velocity outside of 0-127 will be immediately culled

Added some additional websocket response data to the inbound socket. Just in case anyone other than me is listening for response messages over the inbound websocket: the response JSON now contains "display", which informs the server what the current preset or seed is (including edge cases like looping randomize and FMU)

--- CHANGES ---

Moved menu theme buttons from Advanced System > Menu styling to just System > Interface. This means they're accessible in basic mode, and not in a menu nobody in their right mind ever needs to enter

Changed tooltips to be left-aligned rather than centre-aligned, and added a thin border with the current selected button colour around the tooltip to make it more visible. Thanks to Kyrazell for the excellent suggestion!

Changed "Menu styling" to "Advanced menu styling" in System (only visible in advanced mode)

Changed the websocket query function to return the name of the current slot if the current preset was not generated using a random seed, and give a special message if automatic preset randomization is in effect

Changed basic mode note object border "glowing" button to use a value of 4.0 to 8.0 rather than 1.0 to 2.0 for brightness

Changed menu to only update its state when the menu is actually open, and otherwise just cache a pending menu update to be triggered when the menu is opened. This should drastically reduce the overhead for a rapid looping randomizer mode

Changed variable note speed to be a 2-axis graph. This does not auto-convert from old variable max speed + ramping, as I think only a single person has ever used this option, but a 2-axis response gives much better opportunity for cool things like max velocity notes suddenly being way faster

Changed the default "custom angle" to be an offset, perspective angle. Hopefully this can show off the 3D-ness of Keysight to curious button-clickers!

Changed keypress fade out animation curve to be a 2-axis graph. This gives a visual representation of how the keypress will fade without having to actually test it

Changed tooltip default fade-in delay time to 0.75 seconds, and sped up the fade-in animation from 1.0 seconds to 0.5 seconds

Changed note light brightness by velocity to be a 2-axis graph

Changed the name text on pulse and particle system tabs to be an editable text box, to allow for easy and rapid re-naming without going into submenus

Changed note light width slightly (wider for black keys, just a touch wider for white keys) and changed the way the lighting attentuation radius behaves. This should be indistinguishable from older note light behaviour under standard circumstances, but with excessively low concentration or high note height above backdrop, there may be discrepencies

Changed note light concentration slider bounds to be 0.5 to 1.0, although these can be edited down. This is to push users away from using really low note light concentrations, as it has a performance impact and isn't visually consistent in 100% of circumstances

Changed octave lines to always and only use backdrop lighting channel, instead of silently inheriting the overlay lighting channels

Changed particle velocity randomness to use gaussian distribution rather than the default distribution. This fixes the issue of seeing the "range" of paths a particle could take with a high enough spawn rate, as gaussian distribution means that at a randomness of 1.0, ~65% of random values fall within 0.0 to 1.0, 95% of random values fall within -1.0 to 2.0, 99.7% of values fall within -2.0 to 3.0. This means that randomness is now "more random" for the same input value for initial velocity, but the random range is far more natural and you do not see a hard edge at the bounds of particle paths. In testing, old randomness values appear approx 2x more random, so these values have been automatically multiplied down as part of 1.4 preset importing

Changed "Circle (outline)" pulse stencil to be half as thick

Changed "Fade (with speck)" to have a significantly larger centre in proportion to the fade, allowing smaller particles that use this stencil. Particle sizes have been auto-adjusted to compensate by multiplying size by 0.33

Changed impact light fade-out behaviour when in non-sustained-brightness mode. Impact lights now fade out with the given fade-in time, removing the harsh cut while keeping it controllable without additional variables

Changed minimum time dilation to 0.05, down from 0.1

Changed non-sustained note force behaviour to smoothly interpolate down to 0.0 force upon key release, rather than snapping to 0.0 (avoids instant responsiveness on particles, which looked a little odd)

Changed damper block lighting channel from "piano" to "backdrop" (as it looks nicer if they pick up note lights. Impact lights are usually blocked by the keybed divider)

Changed piano key texture unwrapping to use regular top-down mapping rather than custom UV mapping. When textured, the sides of notes might look a little strange, but this gives much greater flexibility in controlling the appearance of textured keys from a normal camera angle

Changed the user-controllable defaults to save to Defaults.sav rather than as part of SystemStruct.sav. This was primarily to avoid struct infrastructure breakdown (hah.) when editing certain low-level structs, but it has the benefit of defaulting everyone's default preset to reflect new 1.4 values too! (As a reminder: this default preset is very important as it is the baseline preset randomized from when using the randomizer)

Removed the "view full documentation in browser" button from the Changelog menu. This was not only wildly outdated, but also tooltips on all buttons within Keysight makes digging through a giant document for information redundant

Removed "key lighting" option. It is far better to use self-emissive materials for keys than to have a directional light on the "piano" light channel blasting at them, and this can now be done via the Basic menu

Removed "cull horizontal" and "cull vertical" global options from Core > Viewport. These are now activated per-particle and per-pulse, for greater flexibility

Removed ability to have CPU-simulated particles. There was never any reason to do this other than if, somehow, GPU particles were not supported on some specific hardware. After gathering some more data in that respect, it seems like not a single computer running Keysight has failed to run GPU particles

Removed some backend internal switching between no-note-wind and note-wind particle system versions based on parameters. The original idea was to have optimised systems based on what is needed, but in practice, the switching is more costly than simply running the un-needed particle modules with 0.00 values

Optimised some internal particle system code. Probably to no perceivable effect, but still!

Optimised texture displacement with notes. As a side effect, global texture displacement with dynamic note speed now makes all notes have the correct texture displacement speed over time (they just all spawn with the same starting offset). Additionally, this fixes a bizarre edge case relating to floating point precision leading to texture displacement speed "desyncing" randomly from notes when Keysight has been open for a long time and/or has a very low time dilation

Optimised material and colour assignment across the project. CPU usage should now be significantly lower unless using dynamic, over-time colours

--- BUG FIXES ---

Fixed notes that are forcibly released by another note spawning from "jumping" one frame's worth of displacement. Rapid notes now look significantly smoother at their origin point as a result

Fixed the no-texture-displacement mode in note object materials. Using non-random mapping and no texture displacement will now properly make notes "reveal" an underlying image

Fixed issue where changing basic mode colour options could set note border colour away from black, if border material is set to blank

Fixed particles and pulses velocity-based activation not functioning

Fixed overlapping pulses and particle slots with translucent material mode from Z-fighting

Fixed new slider UI element doing silly things when being updated to a value greater than the default slider max, or less than the default slider min

Fixed "note light change brightness over time" not working at all in top-down mode. Now, note lights will fade out with note activity once the note reaches it's target location. If you see any bugs with this, let me know, since I get the feeling it's gonna be buggy under some specific circumstances but I couldn't find anything on my end

Fixed toggling frame lighting channels causing white piano plane to appear underneath the piano keys and not go away until a full preset switch is called (SUPER important bug to fix. I expect my Nobel prize nomination in the coming weeks)

Fixed colour hex code display occasionally showing silly things like "#000" instead of the intended "#0F0F0F" when dragging sliders

Fixed note lights having a random black or white key driven width if note objects were disabled

Fixed particle systems not having a new random position within their vector field on repeat note presses, leading to identical particle pathing

Fixed note light brightness being too low when note objects are relatively small. The workaround is a bit of a hack, since it's a delicate balance of attenuation radius/light size/brightness multiplier, but as long as notes are not <0.15cm and concentration is not comically low, note light brightness should be more consistent with small notes (such as those in the default Chopin midi)

Fixed repeat notes causing first impact light to one-frame-flash to its target brightness before being destroyed by the second impact light (highly visible on slow-build impact light setups)

Fixed randomizer not altering default emissive min/max values when randomizing to a transparent material

Fixed normal maps being ever so slightly inaccurate to their intended effect

Fixed note objects with >1 scale from Z-fighting with each other (achieved via a small Z-height offset based on note position. Higher notes now are "on top" of lower notes)

Fixed note lights having a variable brightness when note object scale is changed, and made note light widths exactly the same as note objects

Fixed having large numbers of preset slots potentially tanking CPU performance on weaker systems (for no reason)

Fixed some edge case websocket messages having invalid JSON styling (forgot to escape some characters and crashed my server with it. Whoops! Sorry Adam)

Prospective fix for certain timings of note-on/note-off events causing some effects to become "stuck on" when they shouldn't be

Prospective (second) fix for pedal events sometimes arriving out of order in top-down mode, leading to pedals "stuck down" or not down when they should be

notes.title: Version 1.3.1
notes.content:
Hey guys! Just a small round of fixes and minor additions. Most notably, Cycling colour mode now uses BPM as a speed measurement, and the randomizer only pulls desired custom textures. 

Next major thing to be worked on: retrofitting all old menus with the new graphical editor modules used by Particles, and adding tooltips to everything! As ever, keep the feature requests and usage questions coming in the Steam forums.

Without further ado, here's the changelog for 1.3.1

[h1]Full changelog[/h1]

--- OVERHAULS ---

Custom textures can now have their presence in the randomizer controlled! This means if you import custom textures for a specific preset, those textures (by default) will not appear in the randomizer pool. There are now two folders in the Saved directory that contain textures: the standard /Textures and the new /Textures (randomizer enabled). Placing textures in either will cause them to appear in the menus, but only textures in the randomizer enabled directory will be pulled from in the randomizer. The "open folder" button for textures will point to the non-randomizer-enabled texture path (/Textures)

Changed the Cycling colour mode! Now uses a beats-per-minute measurement for speed rather than an arbitrary value (one beat = one colour slot). Presets will be auto-converted to the new speed values, but you may want to double check any cycling colour presets are behaving as intended

--- SMALL ADDITIONS ---

Added particle shape preview to Basic menu mode particles sub-menu

Added "panic button" to Midi menu, also accessible immediately using the backspace key. This button will remove all current effects and reset all simulation values to their defaults, intended as a backup in case you do something silly like use a 100.0 height area with 0.1 note speed and, several minutes in, decide you don't want to wait another 10 minutes for the note to disappear

--- CHANGES ---

Changed pulses to always multiply the output colour by the pulse stencil colour. This means if you import a custom texture with, say, rainbow stripes and use a white pulse colour, your pulse will be rainbow striped without needing to also specify the texture as an emissive texture overriding the colour

Changed particles to also always multiply by stencil colour in the same way, and deprecated this option in the menu

Changed all text entry fields (except console command field) to consistently apply text entry on focus-move, not just on enter-key. Clicking off text fields will now not give a 50-50 whether that specific field needed an enter-key-press to apply the change!

Slightly altered particle randomization ranges

--- BUG FIXES ---

Fixed non-vsync framerate locking not applying correctly on launch, and being disabled when toggling mask mode

Fixed notes getting "stuck" when rapidly switching between bottom up and top down mode in the setup wizard

Fixed setup wizard midi device selection not updating the selected midi device in the Midi menu, potentially double-binding a midi device and causing issues

Fixed pedal preset switching. As in, it was completely broken, and now it is not broken. Sorry!

Fixed edge case where notes could occupy the same space, and the piano simulation believed the note was not pressed if the engine received a note off + note on event in the same frame. Particle systems may still overlap

Prospective fix for control change events not broadcasting correctly in top-down note mode. Sostenuto/sustain pedals should no longer be "stuck down" sometimes

Prospective fix for colour slots slipping out of sync while using Cycling colour modes (found some bugs as part of overhauling this and fixed them, but there may still be issues)

notes.title: One year anniversary | Keysight 1.3 release!
notes.content:
[h1]Keysight 1.3 is here![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38079779/05140c087e58c2a8a8bbfeaae3c6f101ec373e6c.png[/img]

Welcome to the biggest overhaul of Keysight to date! Featuring: huge visual improvements to particles and the virtual keyboard, smoother performance, deeper piano visualization, stronger streaming tools, and much more. This update has been 5 months in the making, and it is with great joy that it can finally be released into the wild. Go forth, Keysighters, and do cool stuff!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38079779/ffd48d20a3b850f3914e955e9e4345d2386e4249.png[/img]

[h1]Notable new features and improvements[/h1]
[h3]Particles[/h3]
This is the big one. Keysight's particles have always been... fine. Just fine. But other visualizers people are used to seeing have [i]really[/i] nice particles and it was about time Keysight got up to speed! Here are the top level changes:

 - 1,000,000 particles per second cap, up from 100
 - Vector fields and much deeper path customization
 - Force on particles from note events
 - Additional colour modifiers like hue or saturation shift over particle lifetime
 - New graphical-based editing UI
 - Exportable and shareable JSON templates for particle systems

Sounds intimidating? This update ships with 9 finely tuned particle templates and auto-conversion from 1.2 particle systems to 1.3 systems! No need to dig into all the options, simply load up a template and enjoy the huge visual improvements.

[h3]Piano model and animation[/h3]
The 3D models used for piano keys and the frame have gotten a huge facelift. They now support full texturing, are higher resolution, more realistic, and smoothly animate with key events! Complete with subtle key bounce on high-velocity note-off events. On top of this, individual per-key dampers are also visualized and animated, giving a diegetic way of showing pedalling (including sostenuto pedalling!)

[h3]Readable, individual save files[/h3]
Presets are now stored inside individual JSON files! This means presets are more readily shareable, and also human-readable and editable from outside of Keysight itself. Presets can be found by heading into Preset Management and clicking the "Open presets folder" button!

[h3]Mask mode for semi-transparency in OBS[/h3]
Mask mode has gotten a huge overhaul! Gone is the loss of quality and fiddly multi-scene OBS setup nonsense. Mask mode now integrates with an OBS plugin and a single shader filter, as explained in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2362399096]this guide[/url]. It's now completely indistinguishable from non-semi-transparent Keysight in OBS!

[h3]Graphics presets[/h3]
Keysight has always been very resource demanding by default, but with some calibration it can run smoothly on almost any system. The problem has been that these calibration steps are pretty obscure and obtuse, so now they are done for you! Three graphics presets are available in the Graphics menu: "Standard" will give you the best possible visual experience, "Low" is intended for older gaming systems and disables some features like shadow casting and note lights, "Very low" is intended for basic visualization on non-gaming laptops and the like and has all dynamic lighting disabled.

[h3]Default presets[/h3]
Keysight now comes bundled with four default presets, each with three fidelity levels to match the graphics preset chosen. These will be loaded as part of the setup wizard, or via re-selecting a graphics preset in the Graphics tab. This system is very flexible and will be expanded with more default presets in the future!

[h3]More flexible texture system[/h3]
Keysight's default texture sets are now exposed and editable to users inside the install directory, and user-imported normal maps now behave correctly. Also added a bunch more masks and a new texture!

[h3]Better performance and capture[/h3]
Despite all these huge visual improvements to particles/models/shadows, Keysight runs faster and smoother! Average framerate for equivalent presets between 1.2 and 1.3 should be 5-10% improved, but "1% lows" (stutter) is drastically reduced and this now also does not show up in capture software as much.

[h3]Additional element visualizations[/h3]
Pitch bend can now be visualized by wiggling notes from side to side, along with "bending" their hue. Soft pedal can now alter the exposure and bloom of the overall scene to give you a different "feel" when soft pedal is down!

[h3]... and more![/h3]
I know ending a list with "... and more!" is a terrible cliché, but it's true! The full changelog from 1.2.2c to 1.3.0 can be found at the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1325730/view/3019079568363742136]end of this previous announcement[/url]. Warning: it's even more reading than this monster update!

[h1]What's next?[/h1]
 - Better documentation and universal in-Keysight tooltips
 - Upgrading all elements to use the new Graphical Editor UI elements
[b] - Native Twitch chat control[/b] ;)
 - Deeper midi device support and control ID mapping

Here's to one year of the most fun project I have ever worked on, and I am certainly not stopping here! Thank you for making it this far in the post; having folks express interest and share in my passion for music visualization is phenomenally motivating. I hope that I can continue to provide you better and more beautiful tools for your own creative endeavours!

Happy Keysighting <3

notes.title: 1.3.0b on beta branch! - Minor fixes, smoother OBS capture, new mask
notes.content:
Sneaking this one in just before 1.3 goes live on the 24th!

The most important thing in this update is that Unreal Engine's "smoothing" is now disabled. For some context: something that I see a lot on my own streams is that OBS sometimes just completely drops the ball on smooth capture even though Keysight is apparently v-sync locked and running at 60fps. Occasionally, the stream-side Keysight frame pacing will completely tank for around 5-20 seconds before recovering and being silky smooth. After poking around and doing some testing, it seems like disabling Unreal Engine's frame smoothing drastically affects the duration of this "wobble" period, and with smoothing disabled the stream-side pacing recovers from a skipped frame pretty much immediately.

Long story short: smoother OBS capture! Probably.

Anyway, here's the full changelog for other stuff!

[h1]Changelog[/h1]

--- SMALL ADDITIONS ---

Added "Circuit" default mask for all your cyber-y needs!

--- CHANGES ---

Allowed E to hide the setup wizard menu

Disabled Unreal Engine's frame smoothing to (somewhat counter-intuitively) assist in smoother video capture

--- BUG FIXES ---

Fixed midi playback culling in-flight events when midi playback stopped in top-down mode

Fixed "reset to custom angle" not updating piano key size if custom angle did not share the current angle's key length

Fixed some badly wired-up inputs causing E to lower the camera in flycam and left bumper to hide the menu

Fixed Rising Haze and Sandstorm default particle templates trying to use a shape texture that no longer exists

notes.title: 1.3.0a on beta and demo branches! Controller support and improved mask mode
notes.content:
[h2]Hey folks! New update![/h2]

Version 1.3.0a is now available on the beta branch, and via the Steam demo. This version is the one that will be released on the public live branch on [b]June 24th[/b] as part of Keysight anniversary celebrations! Without further ado, here is a summary of the main changes:

 - Mask mode got changed [i]again[/i]. I know I know, I'm sorry, I'm a compulsive mask-mode-er. The overall principle is still the same: using a HLSL shader filter in OBS to achieve nice easy semi-transparency. However, rather than squashing the image and rendering a mask to the other half of the Keysight window, the mask is now encoded into the blue channel of the image without any warping. This gives perfect pixel quality in a way previous mask modes always failed, and on top of this, the way non-masked semi-transparent pixels are displayed is now far more clean and accurate! Check out the guide for updated information on Mask Mode

- Partial controller support! Full disclosure: I added this because I needed it to record a smooth GIF of camera motion for some store page updates, but I was pleasantly surprised at how nice it is to alter the camera angle using controller. 3D camera control, note testing, turbo note test toggling, mask mode toggling, and randomizing are all supported via controller. Check out the Controls menu for a full breakdown! Importantly: menu navigation is [i]not[/i] supported at this time, as none of the menu elements were built with controller focus flow in mind

- Updated some sub-menus, like Controls to reflect the input additions, and Credits to have easy buttons to find the cool streamer people who help me test and refine Keysight! Additionally, the Graphics tab now has graphics preset buttons that will perform the same tasks as the buttons in the setup wizard, i.e. importing default presets, adjusting randomizer weightings and modifying some system graphics settings

- Pulses can now not have any size animation at all. Why? Because somebody wanted to have pulses simply display an image with no further animation for a set amount of time and it was easy to add. "Smallest size" variable in the Pulses menu now controls the proportion of the target size that the pulse will blend away / to, so a value of 1.0 = no animation as both start and end points are the same

Happy Keysighting! And please do keep the feedback and questions coming in the Steam forums, they are invaluable for informing me how best to continue developing <3

[h2]Full changelog:[/h2]

--- OVERHAULS ---

Changed mask mode *again*. This time, mask mode now does not perform any image transforms, and instead encodes the mask switch into the blue channel. This is still intended to integrate with a HLSL shader in OBS, and the links/instructions in the Steam guide have been updated accordingly. Broadly, this will completely fix the pixel sampling issue leading to image quality loss, and the shader has also undergone an upgrade and behaves much more naturally with semi-transparency! You can also use M as a mask mode keyboard toggle, if you want to quickly revert colours back to normal while editing something

Added controller support for some actions! Primarily intended for fly-cam control, but it also includes bindings for randomizing, toggling mask mode, and some other things. Check out the Controls menu for full mapping information

--- SMALLER ADDITIONS ---

Added graphics preset switch buttons to Graphics menu. These will reimport default presets with the correct graphical preset as well as alter the randomizer accordingly, just like the setup wizard does

Added warning to setup wizard that shows when Keysight is not running in a 16:9 aspect ratio, as this can crop or hide some features (notably the entire keyboard when running 21:9)

Added the special console command of "reset" to the System menu. Typing "reset" and pressing enter in the console command field will delete all save data and reboot Keysight, giving a quick way of migrating to a new Keysight version's default settings if save data is not important

Added keyboard hotkey M (or controller right thumbstick click) as a toggle for mask mode

Added "Smallest size" variable to Pulses. This allows pulses to blend to / away from a non-0 size for highly specific pulse implementations, eg having just an image appear on a pulse without any kind of size animation

--- CHANGES ---

Streamlined mask mode options in Advanced Scene > Component visibilities as the additional options are no longer relevant

Changed mask mode to force 100% resolution scale, as the filtering blur from non-native resolution will cause blue fringes around objects in OBS. (If you really want to see this in action, you can enter mask mode and *then* change resolution scale)

Updated the Credits menu, along with adding buttons to easily find the awesome people who helped out!

Updated the Controls menu to show new controller bindings, and be a bit more readable

--- BUG FIXES ---

Fixed default Core settings having a too-high frame-height, allowing notes to completely exit the screen before shrinking back out

Fixed Basic mode randomizer menu buttons generating bad presets when using Low / Very low graphics preset and clicking "randomize safely"

Fixed Polygons normal map having JPEG compression artefacts. Whoops!

Fixed demo mode midi popup pointing user to the System tab to bind a midi device as opposed to the Midi tab

notes.title: NEW PARTICLES! 1.3.0 release candidate on beta branch! - Roadmap update
notes.content:
[h1]It's here![/h1]
HECK. YES. IT'S. DONE. Strap yourselves in, this is going to be one hefty update announcement!

First order of business: this gigantic update is the release candidate for Keysight 1.3.0. This means that nothing much [i]should[/i] change before it moves over to the live branch in a couple of weeks; it is (to the best of my knowledge) stable and feature-complete. 

[b]I highly recommend opting in to the beta branch[/b], this can be done by right clicking on Keysight, heading into Properties > Betas and selecting the beta branch!

[b]I also recommend deleting your save data for Keysight if you have not invested a lot of time in configuration.[/b] Why? Because upon first launch, Keysight's setup wizard now imports a bunch of cool default presets you can use, and auto-configures a ton of graphics options for better performance! Save data is located under [i]Users/[You]/Appdata/Local/Keysight/[/i] simply delete the entire Saved folder.

1.3.0 is the biggest and most complex overhaul I have attempted on the Keysight project thus far, and for the first time I am genuinely proud of some of the systems that are now in-place and useable. Thank you very much for your patience, those of you already on the beta branch and updateless for 2.5 months now... I cannot wait to see what you guys end up building with this and I promise it was worth the wait! Don't forget you can always get in touch directly via the Steam forums, or by tracking me (Egglyberts) down elsewhere on the internet, I actively enjoy talking shop in terms of Keysight feature ideas, implementations and troubleshooting ːsteamthumbsupː

And now. As promised. Walls of text! If you manage read [i]all[/i] of this... I may have to get some sort of medals made.

[h2]Particles[/h2]
Where to even begin on this one... Tell you what, how about a video? Here's all four default presets bundled with this beta, and they showcase particles quite nicely! (Also, whoa, what is that crazy damper visualization at the bottom, huh...)
[previewyoutube=zo3-4_LJ29g;full][/previewyoutube]
So how and why the huge overhaul? Well, particles have always been the weakest part of Keysight, especially when compared to what others are doing with midi visualization in the creative space. Keysight's original particle implementation, that lasted almost a full year, was the most barebones un-researched implementation of the decrepit "Cascade" system in Unreal Engine, just to get something out there. We have now moved over into the exciting new(ish) supercar of real-time VFX: Niagara! The sheer flexibility allowed in Niagara is insane, and it's allowed Keysight to compete (I feel) on visual fidelity while remaining fully controllable by the end-user.

Without further ado, here's an overview of the most exciting new particle features!

[h3]- Note force[/h3]
Simulated piano activity on a note now contributes force on particles! This allows you to "blow around" particles with performance, adding another layer of reactivity to the visuals in a way I was sceptical I could actually achieve. Major thank you to Cellko, who helped immensely with optimising the code required to calculate 88 sources of "gravity" on a [i]per particle[/i] basis in real-time.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38079779/46b97bfded62be30597c266af6c3e6e1ab5e1f02.png[/img]
[h3]- Insane particle spawn counts[/h3]
Know what's lame? A cap of 100 particles per second. Know what isn't? 1,000,000 per second. Try it, if you dare, but I will not be responsible if your graphics card catches fire! More realistically, a mid-range GPU can handle 100k+ particles per second from notes no problem... Niagara really is a hell of a drug. Just be aware that pixel cost scales with the number of transparent surfaces overlaid on top of each other, so having a high particle count and a large particle size will result in drastically reduced framerate. Oh and this screenshot? This is "only" 100k per second
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38079779/74ed8ff87e925d5b3d2e7f351717048a0c243f9c.png[/img]
[h3]- Colour modifiers[/h3]
Particles now take the usual colour settings with 12 slots, but can apply their own per-particle modifiers on top. This means you can have slight hue/sat/val randomization per particle, particles that flicker over time, particles that change colour over the course of their lifetime... or all of these at once!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38079779/8374f8f8f622116ad0983946ec01f9bff4b8f89b.png[/img]
[h3]- New editing UI[/h3]
Hoo boy. Sounds like a lot of options? It is. A single particle system now has something like 120+ variables, which would have been an absolute nightmare of sliders under the previous menu styling. Graphical editors to the rescue! Inspired by filter envelope editors in DAWs, the new particle system menu uses a fresh UI module I call the Graphical Editor. This contains 5 pieces of primary data: when the effect starts; how strong the effect is when it starts; when the effect ends; how strong the effect is when it ends; and the curvature between those points. These are edited visually by clicking and dragging handles on a graph! It also comes with a "reset" button, configurable min/max value ranges, and a toggle to use just a single value instead of a min/max curve.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38079779/45d2dbdf1dafbc07bc59a26721484715a1dd7b07.png[/img]
[h3]- Absolute control[/h3]
Did I mention the 120+ variables? And how there's A LOT OF VARIABLES?! Because there is, and it is a lot. We have moved away from the old "pick your path, apply some modifiers to it", now YOU design the particle path. This is done through an array of initial velocities, accelerations-over-particle-lifetime, acceleration-by-note-velocity, drag, vector fields, note force influences... it's a long list. I am not even sure what the limits of this new system are, so go forth, brave adventurers! Find out!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38079779/54a5dd04b37dc9c16c0de088a6925cefcbacc750.png[/img]
[h3]- Templates[/h3]
Oh, you err, don't wanna edit 120 variables and make your own particle paths..? Weird, but ok. Fortunately, I am actually aware enough to make affordances for this! Enter: Templates. These are collections of particle systems saved to a single JSON file, with a name / author / description, that can be easily loaded and applied to any preset. The particle system menu now has a small disabled-by-default toggle in the top right called "use full template editor" when in Advanced menu mode. While this is disabled, only variables that have been flagged as "exposed" are shown under sub-tabs, which means templates can restrict the options to only the intended, relevant ones! While template mode is enabled, every single setting is exposed (along with the flags to mark variables as exposed for non-template users) and the export settings to save out the current particle loadout to a JSON. I hope this goes some way to obfuscating just how complex particles have become, while still allowing anyone to take full advantage of it all!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38079779/831f77d007f82090bb43f4e50b084a3fc7ba4a93.png[/img]

[h2]Mask Mode[/h2]

Ahhh the problem child of Keysight options. Never quite been happy with this one, but it's much better than it was! Mask mode is now intended to integrate with a HLSL shader filter in OBS, vastly simplifying the masking process and bringing with it some visual benefits. No more alpha spill due to bloom spilling over the border, no dark fringing, configurable note/semi-transparency visibility! [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2362399096]Check out the guide[/url] on how to make Keysight semi-transparent in OBS. Also has new split modes! If you have a monitor with more resolution "headroom" than your target Keysight resolution (eg. 4k monitor but running Keysight at 1080p), you can remove stretching and instead mirror the render for masking across the horizontal or vertical centre lines to maintain perfect pixel quality.

[h2]Performance and smoothness[/h2]

A ton of back-end data handling and effect spawning code has been reworked in this beta! In testing, with the default launch preset that Keysight is shipped with, performance has gone up by around 5-10% for the most part since 1.2.2c (while now looking significantly nicer), [i]however[/i]: stability and performance under spikes of load are now significantly improved! Glissandos will still absolutely tank your framerate, but not nearly as far as previously. Err, please don't kill your computer trying to run black midi through Keysight just yet though.

Additionally, capture smoothness in OBS should be improved thanks to reworking the way thread syncing and v-syncing works in Keysight. Enabling v-sync will now add noticeably more input latency (up to about 100ms), but the benefit is that OBS is less likely to randomly poop itself and drop frames despite Keysight being at a smooth 60 if v-sync is on.

[h2]Textures[/h2]

The way textures load, both from users and by Keysight itself, has changed significantly! Default textures were previously baked directly into the Keysight packaged program, with user textures loading from files placed manually inside the install directory. Now, Keysight loads default textures from folders and files visible to the user inside the Keysight install (specifically /Keysight/Default textures), and user textures are loaded from Appdata, to keep it consistent with the new preset save location!

This brings with it some less immediately apparent but huge benefits: default texture sets are used by the randomizer, so previously you could not randomize to a full material set that was not baked into the engine. By adding files to the default textures folder yourself, you can flesh out Keysight's "default texture" sets yourself! Conversely, as an end-user you can now remove default textures if you never want to see them again (like, I dunno... cushion).

In order to do this, you will need to add an image to each of the Colour / Metal / Roughness / Specularity / Normal map folders [i]with the same name[/i]. Keysight requires the same-named thing to build up a full material with all texture slots filled for usage in the randomizer, and for the "apply to all slots" button to work.

Particle and pulses also use independent stencil pools, and these have been slightly updated, along with some new masks and a new default material being added!

[h2]Default presets and configuration[/h2]

As part of the setup wizard, Keysight now pulls and installs some default presets from the install files and auto-configures graphics options! If you're an existing user wanting to take advantage of these, you have two options: 

- (Recommended) wipe your save data. Like, actually. If you have no presets you care deeply about, the fastest way of getting all the new pre-made configuration and presets is to get Keysight to set itself back up again from scratch. Save data lives in /Appdata/Local/Keysight/Saved, you can get to Appdata by typing in %appdata% into the Windows search bar. Delete the entire Saved folder and launch Keysight to wipe and rebuild saves (be warned, this does wipe the Stats.sav file, so back that up if it's important to you).

- (Advanced) launch Keysight once so it generates the new save file locations, and then navigate to the Keysight Steam install. Inside the Keysight folder you will find "default presets", simply copy the JSONs from the desired graphics preset subfolder to your Appdata/Local/Keysight/Saved/Presets save location and reload presets in Keysight from the Preset Management tab.

This setup process also has much more useful and robust graphics preset options than before! Selecting between Standard/Low/Very low will update the default presets accordingly, as well as change some system settings and randomizer settings to ensure consistent performance. If you're on a weaker system, using Low or Very low should give you a [i]much[/i] better experience, without losing too much visual quality!

[h2]Other cool stuff[/h2]

[b]Pitch bend visualisation![/b] Pitch bend now can both horizontally shift notes and hue-shift their colour. By default, notes are moved up/down two semi-tones in position and hue-shifted by 60 degrees around a colour wheel, but these parameters are (you guessed it) configurable.

[b]Soft pedal visualisation![/b] While not the most ideal way of visualising soft pedal, there is now a disabled-by-default option in Viewport for multiplying the render exposure and bloom multiplier while the soft pedal is depressed. This was in an attempt to show the "colour shift" by using soft pedal during performance, but it applies as a blanket modifier rather than per-note, so it isn't necessarily totally accurate to the sound feel unless you're using the soft pedal as a binary tonal switch for segments of music (which, err, I personally do a lot. Bad habit). The better way of visualising soft pedalled notes already exists though: it's the pedal preset mapping option under Hotkeys, although this of course requires forethought and manual setup versus a global modifier.

[b]Time offsets for pulses![/b] Ever wanted a collapsing ring pulse to happen [i]before[/i] a note event in top-down mode? No? Not surprised, but I wanted this, so I built it! You can now arbitrarily time-offset pulses in either direction, although obviously you need to be in top-down mode to use ahead-of-note-on time offsets. We can't violate causality with Keysight juuust yet and do that in real-time...

[b]New material and masks![/b] Added the "Polygons" default material, along with "polygonal" and "cracks" masks. Particularly happy with the Polygons material, does a great job at being icy or synthwave-y.

[h1]Roadmap update[/h1]

Back in the hazy distant past of February, I included a little roadmap segment and I would like to update and amend my plans. As ever, I'm a one-man dev-team with constantly shifting interests and no shareholders or E3 trailers to make me actually DO specific things, so the following represents my plans at the time of writing and may not be accurate in the future! With that disclaimer out of the way:

We did it! Particles got overhauled. Phew. This was the biggest pain point for me personally, as Keysight's particles always looked kinda bad by comparison to what others in the space were doing.

We didn't do it! Native Twitch integration is not going to be part of the Keysight 1.3 release, despite me talking about this in the earlier roadmap update. A lot of groundwork has been laid here, but it's still a giant task and I underestimated how deep I would get into the particle systems and other feature reworks for 1.3, so Twitch integration is going to be pushed to a "1.4" release.

As part of pushing Twitch integration into a 1.4 release, I would like to theme the next round of updates around community and usability. Now that we have JSON file based presets, why not make them super easy to share around? To that end, I would love to build some sort of easily accessible and fully integrated repository of presets. I am envisioning a menu tab in Keysight called "Community" with just a big old list of presets that other folks have made and shared, and you can perform a one-click install to your current preset slot. This would then be potentially expandable to things like particle system templates!

I would also like to revisit piano activity simulation. Keysight, currently, internally calculates a linear dropoff of... let's call it "string energy" over time, and then an exponent (typically 1.5) is applied to this to generate a dropoff curve for various effects like impact light brightness, or velocity sensitivity if enabled etc. Now, I'm sort of obsessive about wanting to showcase every detail of what is happening musically via the visuals, and I am unhappy with the lack of control and accuracy this system has at actually representing the string energy in piano. I need to do more research and testing on precisely how the energy in a string swells and decays over time based on note position on a piano, and based on velocity, but this system has been targeted for a rework.

Also long-due another revision: automation, hotkeys and websockets. The entire system for triggering certain actions from a websocket trigger or hotkey trigger is abysmal. I've run into it a bunch of times myself where "load from file" is pointing at a [i]slot index[/i] and not an actual preset name, so if presets have been reshuffled it'll grab the wrong file. I have a million ideas for making these systems much more usable and robust, but they're all super dull UX things so I'll not spend any more time talking about them other than to say IT'LL BE BETTER SOON, I PROMISE

Tooltips. Keysight actually has them! At least, it has them in random places with a varying amount of usefulness. As part of a commitment to better guides and documentation, I would like to perform The Great Tooltip-ening sooner rather than later. This may be part of back-porting the new slider and grpahical editors into older menus, as these UI elements have nice easy tooltip entry points. Having tooltips giving a general explanation of what each option does should definitely help the user experience, I know a lot of the options are reeeeally niche and difficult to intuit.

Some final random things on my prospective to-do list:
- Per midi-channel, per-control-ID control ID remapping (for drumkit visualization and stuff)
- Visual overlays like a refractive rain layer
- "Ambient" particle systems, so the background can always have little sparks and embers floating around
- Rework midi device handling (that code is ancient and... bad)
- Video renderer..? ;)

[h1]The entire, huge changelog from version 1.2.2c to version 1.3.0[/h1]

--- Changes from 1.2.2c to 1.3.0 ---

This changelog is going to be pretty huge, as it covers an entire beta cycle with 5 preview builds. Starting off, overhauls! 

--- OVERHAULS ---

Overhauled the piano and frame model! Black keys are more accurately positioned, shape and gaps between keys are true to real pianos, frame shape has been updated (based on a Roland FP-30 style, for the most part). Piano keys can also take the advanced material mode, ie have textures assigned, and have an option for a realistic inner wooden material enabled by default

Overhauled effect spawning system! Lower CPU and memory usage across the board, with potential for much greater flexibility down the line

Overhauled mask mode. Mask mode now has near-zero performance impact! It also integrates with OBS in a different way, using a single shader file (thank you, Cellko) to handle masking rather than the clunky multiple scene approach used previously. Please refer to the Steam guide on mask mode on upgrading to the new masking setup! Other improvements brought with this overhaul include less dark fringing around objects, selectable visibility on notes and semi-transparency, different image splitting modes, toggle for anti-aliasing the stencil, and more!

Overhauled presets to use the JSON data format! This is a huge one, as it allows much simpler sharing of individual presets, and human readability (to some degree, anyway) of preset files directly in a text editor (Visual Studio Code is recommended). Presets are now saved to “../Appdata/Local/Keysight/Saved/Presets” Additionally, any time a save function is called, all current saved files will be moved to the "../Appdata/Local/Keysight/Saved/Presets (backup)" folder before new saves are written. This gives one level of emergency backup, should anything go wrong in the save process or save was called accidentally. I still encourage everyone to make manual backups of save files if you have presets you care deeply about!

Overhauled particle systems! Not sure where to even begin with this one, but broadly:
 - Particles now use a single, universal system with a TON of configuration and simulate on the GPU
 - Particles are loaded from templates (JSON-based!)
 - Multi-system 'templates' can be created inside Keysight, including setting which variables are visible to "normal" users
 - Particles no longer have a limit on their spawn count (well, err, technically I did lock it to 1,000,000 per second. Which is a lot more than 100)
 - Particles can have a force applied to them by note events across the keyboard
 - Particles can have vector field force applied, giving those nice wiggles
 - Particles can have colour modifiers attached, like hue-shift over time or random brightness
 - Particle editing uses the new "graphical editor" module and data structure! FEWER sliders, more useability, more options!

Overhauled texture system! Previously, engine-default full-material texture sets were baked into Keysight. Now they load from the Keysight/Default textures folder in the install directory, by searching any found Colour images against matching named images in all other material channel folders
 - By adding textures to all Default textures material sub-folders with the same name, end-users can now add new full materials and have these appear in the randomizer
 - By deleting textures from Default textures sub-folders, end-users can now stop materials (like, for example, Cushion) from appearing in the randomizer. Being sent to the Leatherbound Dimension is now opt-out!
 - Additionally, pulses and particles now use different texture pools for stencils. No more giant spinning cogs because a pulse got randomized to a snowflake particle stencil!

Overhauled "alternate frame sync" toggle in Graphics. This is now the low-latency toggle, and is part of a larger back-end change to thread syncing and v-syncing. Ultimately, using in-Keysight v-sync will now have around 100ms of input lag, but Keysight runs 30+% faster in CPU-bound situations, and runs significantly smoother in capture software like OBS. Disabling vsync or using the low-latency toggle restores old behaviour, if you need instant responsiveness for whatever reason (or just hate "sticky sliders" from the input lag)

Overhauled pooling system. Should assist in CPU performance when lots of stuff is happening at once

Overhauled setup wizard, and default presets! If you have previous save data you don't really care about, I would highly recommend wiping everything under Appdata/Local/Keysight/Saved and starting fresh, as the setup wizard now comes with a ton of awesome default presets, and much more robust and useful graphics preset options. Graphics presets also auto-adjust the Randomizer to ensure randomizing does not re-able expensive, unwanted effects. Default presets also run significantly faster than previous default settings, thanks to tuning some lighting variables

--- SMALLER ADDITIONS ---

Added piano key randomization support for Advanced material type

Added damper visualization! Enabled by default, found under Scene > Visibilities

Added realistic key animations! Complete with bounce on fast note-off events

Added sostenuto pedal simulation to note activity simulations!

Added piano felt colour option

Added lighting channel response options to frame

Added midi event log to Midi menu to assist in debugging any strange midi behaviour, or dial in piano simulation variables

Added option to Graphics for controlling shadow quality (maps to r.Shadow.MaxResolution 256 / 512 / 1024 / 2048 / 4096 / 8192, not recommended to use 8192, 1024 was the previous default)

Added option to Graphics for post-process image sharpening

Added a new "system alerts" splash screen displaying any messages from actions like automatically importing old saves

Added randomization for impact light candle flicker variables, not just the toggle

Added shape option to pulse settings to reflect mask option in pulse material settings (to more easily control pulse shape without digging into material settings)

Added v-sync syncing interval slider. This number is the divisor against monitor refresh rate to give v-synced framerate (so sync interval = 2 gives 30fps on a 60hz monitor, or 60fps on a 120hz monitor)

Added key animation speed slider under advanced Core > Viewport

Added CPU simulation switch to particles. Warning: do not use this unless you have to, for some reason! GPU simulations allows for much faster performance, and higher particle counts

Added "Cracks" and "Polygonal" engine-default masks

Added "Polygons" default material

Added a "Suppress midi warning" midi device to always appear in the midi device dropdown. This will get rid of the watermark warning about not having a midi device bound, if you simply want to do midi file related things with Keysight

Added pitch bend support! Found under Advanced menu Core > Piano Simulation, pitch bend will shift the note object horizontally by up to 2 semi-tones in either direction, as well as hue-shift the colour by 60 degrees by default. Both of these options are fully configurable

Added soft pedal visualization! This is applied as a whole-scene blanket visual effect, as more fine-tuned soft-pedal preset switching on a per-note basis is already possible under Hotkeys > Pedal preset switching. Soft pedal visualization is disabled by default, and found under Advanced Core > Viewport. While soft pedal is depressed, scene exposure will be multiplied down but bloom will be multiplied up over the given time, giving a fuzzy, dimmer temporary look

Added arbitrary positioning and rotation for the keybed! This allows for a horizontal keybed and a vertical visualization (by rotating keybed 90 degrees, removing camera tilt and local roll, and flying around for a good angle). Primarily intended for assisting augmented-reality style effects in conjunction with mask mode, but could potentially be used for just interesting angles under default operation

Added link to mask mode guide on Steam next to the mask mode toggle in Component visibilities

Added "time offset" to pulse objects. This allows pulses to spawn ahead or behind note events (obviously you're gonna need top-down mode for pulses spawning before notes, we can't violate causality with Keysight juuust yet). Collapsing rings ahead of note impacts and then expanding mist pulses look great!

Added websocket trigger for remotely changing the camera angle used in Keysight. This works in much the same way as the seed randomization, where the assigned trigger word is expected along with a colon, and then anything to the right is treated as data. The data format for camera information is as follows: {"x":58.45,"y":-48.62,"z":72.01,"tilt":-43.06,"rotate":0,"roll":-38.03,"localRoll":90,"FOV":65.00} and correct usage would be a trigger word of “camera” and a websocket message of “camera:{"x":58.45,"y":-48.62,"z":72.01,"tilt":-43.06,"rotate":0,"roll":-38.03,"localRoll":90,"FOV":65.00}” obviously substituting in your intended camera values

--- CHANGES ---

Changed piano simulation in the upper register. At Ab6 and above, note activity is calculated using sustain lifetime even if not sustained (as notes on a real piano do not have dampers up on these strings)

Changed randomizer chance generation ***all old seeds now give different results, sorry!*** Disabling or editing randomizer branch options will no longer impact other branches

Changed dynamic shadow casting settings. Shadow resolutions are now much higher and smoother by default!

Changed randomizer update function to only call necessary updates, rather than calling the entire preset update stack. This should reduce the chance of frame stutter during extremely fast loop randomizing

Changed how global core settings work in the data-handling sense. Core settings will need to be rebuilt by the user, but no functionality has changed

Changed some default settings, notably key length to showcase the new piano model a little more (sue me.)

Changed wording on some setup wizard warnings

Changed setup wizard to not save newly created save references until wizard is completed, avoiding edge case where user closes Keysight (or Keysight crashes) mid-setup and does not automatically see the wizard again after re-launching

Changed midi device setup wizard screen to have a button that directly opens the Steam guide relating to midi device mirroring

Changed slider appearance in Dark and Keysight menu themes to be much more visible. Switch menu to Advanced, head into System > Menu Style and reselect your desired preset to update the styling if you have existing saves

Changed piano plane to not render to the stencil channel during mask mode. If using piano plane instead of piano keys in the keybed portion of Keysight, disabling frame visibility and enabling mask mode will now only show the lighting on the piano plane (rather than masking it out)

Changed preset manipulators (the tabs for each preset in Preset Management). Text entry is now overlaid on top of the selection toggle, and save/load icons are hidden except on the selected preset

Changed Viewport and Component visibilities tabs to have some more spacing and subheadings for each major section. These probably need to move to subtabs eventually, the menus are getting kinda huge

Changed randomizer to first apply the defaults-calibration preset to the active preset and then randomize from there, rather than taking whatever is in-use and randomizing. This means if you're running very specific settings for a preset that are not touched by the randomizer (such as impact light falloff amount), randomizing will default these values rather than leave them in place. WARNING: if your default preset is "use global core" but your current preset is "use preset settings", randomizing may alter the active core settings via defaulting this switch (as the switch exists per-preset)

--- BUG FIXES ---

Fixed ambient brightness text having broken mouse-over text

Fixed "cull horizontal" text not being bound to specified menu style text colour

Fixed "refresh midi files" causing duplicate midi devices to appear in midi device menu in Midi tab

Fixed "midi device not bound" warning pointing the user to System menu, when midi devices are now bound under the Midi menu

Fixed camera Z location input defaulting to 1.0 if clicking on the text entry field and then clicking off

Fixed "disable websocket actions" websocket action from sending response message "unrecognized command" despite being recognized and executed

Fixed keypress indicators fading out badly when animating horizontal/vertical fades. Axis-based fades are now performed as an alpha mask rather than a model scale

Fixed mask mode not applying correctly on Keysight launch

Fixed flycam failing to update camera angle variables while in global core mode

Fixed flycam toggling not updating cursor visibility correctly under all circumstances

Fixed user-defined custom angle not saving / applying at all

Fixed websocket triggers being case sensitive

Fixed reloading textures clearing selected option in particle menus for particle shape

Fixed normal maps just having... completely broken normals. Amazing how this one flew under the radar, but normal map influenced surface angles are now not backwards and inverted in the horizontal channel

Fixed Basic colour menu sliders from being horribly unresponsive/laggy

Fixed (?) pedals getting "stuck". Hard to verify this one on my own, as I've only seen it happen twice and I have no way of forcing the behaviour, but a prospective fix is in place. If you have this issue, let me know about it!

Fixed incorrect activity simulation while animate keys was set to false

Fixed colour picker sliders causing unnecessary update function calling while snapping mode was enabled. This should make certain colour pickers far more responsive

Removed midi device selector from System menu (use the one in the Midi tab)

Removed saving and loading from DonorPreset.sav as presets can now be shared much more directly via individual JSONs
