notes.title: Version 1.3.0 Preview 1 in beta branch! - Roadmap update
notes.content:
[h1]Hey, hi and hello! New things![/h1]

Let's jump right into it. First up, piano simulation improvements! Here's a video:
[previewyoutube=NoH7op0_SM8;full][/previewyoutube]

As you can see, a bunch of work has been done on key animations and general piano simulation. I've been wanting to incorporate some sort of pedalling display into Keysight for a long time, and the good-idea fairy finally struck with "what if we just model the dampers?". I know few people care about pedalling to the extent of wanting to show it pretty front-and-centre, so it's disabled by default. Head into Advanced menu mode and Scene > Visibilities to enable dampers. You can also control the material of the dampers, using a semi-transparent black material and disabling felt triangles can make the damper-bar nice and subtle.

In relation to piano animation: piano keys now animate with velocity! Complete with key-bounce on return, if the note-off velocity is high enough. Piano keys also richer material control, an inner wood material, and vastly improved models. Previously, piano keys were simple blocks that clipped into each other when depressed... now, piano keys have all 8 different shapes as found on a real piano! Oh, and the frame model got updated and has lighting channel response support. And piano felt was added. With colour control. Now you too can be one of those weirdos with green piano felt!

Another major change: the randomizer's chance generation has been altered. In version 1.2.0, changing colour randomization settings would have a knock-on effect for the rest of the randomization, as the whole thing used a single incrementing seed. Now, each randomizer branch has its own sub-seed generated from the master seed, so changing randomizer chance branch weights will not impact generation of other categories. This is to make known-good seed values a little more widely applicable over any streams with chat integration! But err, in the process, all old seeds now generate differently.

Oh, and there's a bunch of small fixes, edits and general quality of life things added. Check the changelog for a full list!

To access the beta branch, right click on Keysight in your Steam library, head into Properties > Betas and select "Beta" from the dropdown. Windows-only, this beta is using an experimental plugin for a few secret sauce back-end things which is not compiled for Mac OS just yet.

[h1]Roadmap update[/h1]

It's been a while since talking about plans, so I'm gonna continue with the absolute WALL of text that is this announcement and give a little update! 1.3.0 is gonna be a pretty juicy update when it's all wrapped up. I want to achieve the following "big goals":
[list]
[*] - Piano simulation improvements to support sostenuto pedal and more accurate note activity ***DONE!***

[*] - Piano model and animation improvements for fancy close-up angles ***DONE!***

[*] - Natively supported Twitch chat integration

Keysight's greatest ability is its potential as a stream-integrated visualiser. Using websockets, it's already possible to have chat-controlled Keysight, but despite the wonderful guide written by a community member, it remains an intimidating prospect to set up a Socket IO server and all the chat-reading things. I would like to set up a global KeysightBot Twitch account and a Twitch tab inside Keysight where you can dial in chat control and just have it... work. As a fair warning, I am intending to charge a $5/month subscription for this element of Keysight (handled through Steam's recurring subscription stuff). Fear not though, manual websockets are not going anywhere!

[*] - Particle system rework

It's been a VERY long time overdue. Keysight's particles might be the weakest part of the visualisation when compared to its visualiser peers, and I want to flip that around. The details are still a little conceptual at this point, I suspect it's going to be quite a fight with the particle systems in Unreal Engine, but I would like particles to be much more modular on the per-system level than they currently are. Instead of selecting a path type, and then slapping in some additional vector field magic or whatever to make them look cooler (which was my original plan), Basic mode will have preset paths and Advanced mode will give you control over all the acceleration and velocity over time elements. Want particles to have gravity? Just add some negative Y axis acceleration. That sort of thing. This rework will also allow for more particles per second from each system, the current solution for randomising particle pathing limits the effective number of particles per second you can really have, as they start occupying the same space as each other.
[/list]

There's some bad news though: adding all these new features, I've been running into more and more strange behaviour in relation to data handling, and may need to completely rework how preset data is saved. It shouldn't impact anything on the user side, but it might take a loooong time to fix since every. single. reference. to a variable would need to be rewired. 

If you're still, somehow, hungry for news and discussion of Keysight, feel free to ask me about it [url=https://www.twitch.tv/egglyberts]on-stream[/url] or in [url=https://discord.gg/qYNJWpp58y]discord![/url]

notes.title: Hotfix - Version 1.2.2a
notes.content:
So err, I done goofed, whoops! All fixed now. An explanation, in case you noticed anything weird going on:

As part of the recent update, a ton of back-end variables had their default values changed. This caused some buttons to set the wrong variable upon being clicked. For example, as the previous default note shape was "semi-rounded", and the new default note shape is "rounded", the "semi-rounded" button was actually saying "set the note shape to be [default note shape]" and not specifically "semi-rounded". So once the default was updated, a ton of buttons pointed to the wrong thing! I find it highly amusing I got away with such a glaring bug for four days without anyone noticing, randomizer OP.

Changelog:

Fixed a ton of menu buttons incorrectly setting their relevant variable (eg. colour mode "static setting colour mode to "key position")

Fixed resolution dropdown to correctly update to show (or not show) the current resolution as the dropdown selected resolution after applying resolution settings

notes.title: Midi file support - Version 1.2.1 now live!
notes.content:
[h1]Happy new year![/h1]

Starting off 2021 the right way, with much requested Keysight features! This is a pretty small update, but a very important one.

Keysight can now import and play back midi files! No messing around with external bits of software, just stick your midi file in the Midi folder and you can play it back from the new menu tab. The Midi menu also contains options for midi playback speed, and can be linked to a thing I like to call "time dilation".

Time dilation is accessible via the advanced Core menu, or by keeping midi playback speed linked to time dilation and editing playback speed. This value will act as a speed modifier across all objects and effects in Keysight (and update in real-time, which makes it a fun slider to play with). 

The idea behind adding time dilation is to facilitate smoother offline content for Youtube. If you play back a midi file at 0.25x speed and then speed the video capture back up in editing to its original duration, the resulting video should be more reliably a perfect 60fps regardless of how crazy your preset is!

There's also a couple of minor bug fixes, as follows

[h1]Changelog[/h1]

Fixed turbo note testing mode forcing manual note test to be released instantly

Fixed date display in stats menu showing silly things like "12:2". Again.

Fixed bottom cap of "rounded" shape black keys from not casting shadow from impact lighting with default camera settings

Fixed turbo note testing mode generating a second note-on event on control IDs that are already active (fixes flickering keypresses primarily)

Changed behaviour of Mask Mode. Now does not interfere with standard Keysight operation (can still use menus etc)

Added native midi file playback! Place midi files inside Keysight/Keysight/Midi

Added time dilation function to Core menu (advanced only)

notes.title: Major overhaul - Version 1.2.0 now live!
notes.content:
[h1]Season's greetings![/h1]

Keysight has long suffered from a cramped and horrible-to-use menu. What started as a "oh, let's rework the menu" turned into a full systems rebuild, because the menu should really point to cleaner-structured variables, right? And then 4 months disappeared. But hey, got it done in time for Christmas!

Almost every single aspect of Keysight got rebuilt from the ground up to support a new data structure for presets. The exciting thing here is not the smattering of cool new features that got added in the process, but the flexible way in which new features can be added down the line. 2021 will be an exciting year for midi visualization, and that's a promise.

Anyway, I hope you all have a wonderful Holiday! Without further ado, here are the update details... brace for impact, wall of text incoming!

[h1]Major feature reworks[/h1]

 - Re-structured, re-stylable menu.

 - Infinite preset slots, improved back-end

 - "Pulse" objects replacing rings

 - Custom particle and pulse textures

 - Seed-based randomizer

 - Support for dynamic masking for perfect semi-transparency, no chroma key required

 - Improved auto camera adjustment, first person cam, dolly zoom FOV slider

 - Improved performance

 - Individual note stat tracking

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
(Advanced menu only - Basic menu is simply organised into tabs for the most part)

[h2]Important overhauls[/h2]

Re-structured menu. Menu now follow a tab-based approach. Various menu behaviours can be controlled via the System > Interface tab. Holding alt while interacting with a slider will disable value snapping.

'Rings' have been changed to 'Pulses'. These perform the same basic function, but are modular with infinite slots available; use a texture-based shape (with user-imported texture support); and have a configurable activation / rotation / brightness.

Presets are now infinite, and are saved to a single PresetsStruct.sav in AppData/Local/Keysight/Saved/SaveGames. Preset management tab can be used to "export" the currently selected preset to DonorPreset.sav, for sharing single presets.

[h2]Core menu[/h2]

Fixed a lot of weird edge-case behaviour relating to changing top-down / bottom-up note mode while notes are active

Moved camera settings from Graphics Settings to "Viewport" tab

Moved "animate piano keys" to Viewport tab

Changed "use global core" toggle to be more obvious

Changed key length edits to also affect frame height if frame height is default value

Changed field of view slider to perform a "dolly zoom" effect when in a default camera angle to keep the active area framed

Added "reset to custom angle" option, and a button to save the current camera angle as "custom angle"

Added "alignment image overlay" feature. Allows for a user-imported image to be applied across the screen with variable opacity to facilitate camera matching. Images are imported under "Camera alignment" custom texture folder. Also has alignment notes spawn option (spawns low A + all C notes)

Added sustain pedal midi velocity floor and ceiling sliders

[h2]Effects menu[/h2]

[h3]Note Objects[/h3]

Added shape override. This forces all notes to use the shape of the override, regardless of which key is actually being activated

Added width and depth scaling for white and black key objects. Width scale applies additional X-axis scaling, depth provides additional Z-axis scaling (ie scaling towards the camera)

[h3]Note lights[/h3]

Changed "min brightness" to now be a proportion of the maximum brightness

[h3]Keypresses[/h3]

Added fade-out animation curve slider. High values give sharp change at the beginning of animation, and less at the end

Added opacity fade and horizontal shink animation options, with toggles to enable/disable animation types independently

[h3]Impact lights[/h3]

Changed "min radius" to now be a proportion of the maximum radius

Added option to enable/disable impact light brightness being dependent on sustain pedalling

Added option to control Y-axis shift of impact light

Added option to control light falloff exponent. Higher values cause sharper lighting dropoff. Low values might look better on metallic backdrops

[h3]Pulses[/h3]

These replace the previous "ring" objects! See documentation for full option breakdown

[h3]Particles[/h3]

Changed all "min" values except brightness to be "min proportion". "Fade-out" speed option is now "Min speed prop. on note-off", and controls the proportion of minimum speed particles blend to once key is released and particles are still in flight

[h2]Scene menu[/h2]

Added "masking mode" feature to "Component visibilities" tab. This allows for semi-transparency in OBS using the StreamFX plugin's Dynamic Mask filter rather than using chroma-keying. See documentation and Steam guide for more information

[h2]Randomizer menu[/h2]

Fixed a ton of specific edge-case randomization bugs and unintended behaviours

Overhauled randomizer to use "seed" values. Clicking "randomize" generates a random number to be used as a seed before performing randomization, or a seed can be specified and randomized with for a guaranteed random preset. Only alphanumeric characters are parsed into seed values

Added minimum / maximum hue sliders for colour randomization, for randomizing to specific colour sets. Min hue locks hue values to the right of the slider position, "wrapping back around" if max hue is lower than min hue

[h2]Hotkeys menu[/h2]

Changed debug testing notes to spawn with the actively selected preset if using midi channel preset switching mode, allowing testing of changes to the current preset without having to generate notes over that specific midi channel

Added support for more actions to be automated through hotkeys

Added option to keep backdrop and piano materials as the default materials (specified under System > Defaults Calibration) while in automatic randomization mode, to ensure backdrop does not "flash" due to excessive switching with low interval

Removed option for "preset cycle" and "preset random" automatic switching options. If you are a user who wants these features back, get in touch! (They got removed because nobody used them, as best I could tell)

[h2]Graphics menu[/h2]

Added options to enable alternate frame delivery mode. Basically a placebo button, I have no idea what it does

[h2]System menu[/h2]

Added "Interface" menu tab with options to tune menu behaviour

Added "password" and "command" fields for Inbound Websocket connectivity. See documentation for more information

Added override switch for Inbound Websocket to disable incoming commands from having any effect

Added "Menu styling" menu tab for switching between menu themes (or if you're really obsessive, customizing the look of every button in Keysight)

Added "Default material calibration" menu tab to override defaults used when Keysight spawns new pulses, particles, presets etc.

Added button to re-run Setup wizard

[h2]Statistics menu[/h2]

Added support for showing every note tracked individually. Mouse over each bar for specific counts

[h2]Changelog menu[/h2]

Added changelog menu to view update information directly from inside Keysight

[h2]Other changes[/h2]

Changed how first-person fly camera (activated with F) behaves. Now is more similar to free-cams in video games. Changing camera tilt to 0 degrees and local roll to 0 will functionally "flip" Keysight "upright", to behave like a TV hanging on a wall

notes.title: Version 1.2.0 beta now available!
notes.content:
"Oh, let's just rework the menus to be a little nicer to use". Two months and an entire project overhaul later, it's time to share the progress!
[h1]Accessing the beta[/h1]
New features are available in the beta branch of Keysight. These can be accessed by right clicking on Keysight in your Steam library, heading into Properties, then the Betas tab, and selecting "beta -" from the drop-down list. If Keysight does not automatically update, uninstalling and reinstalling will force Steam into giving you the right files immediately.

[b]PLEASE NOTE that while your old save files will not be touched (other than Stats.sav), neither will they be used. You will need to set up all your configuration within the beta from the ground up.[/b] The public, main release will include a translation layer between old and new presets. Any settings created in the beta version of 1.2.0 will carry into the main release of 1.2.0, and old presets will be imported into 1.2.0 when it is released even if you have used the beta. 

[h1]New features and changes overview[/h1]
I'll try to keep the overview as brief as possible: as part of reworking menus, I ended up touching on and reworking almost every aspect of Keysight. The following are the most exciting changes:

- Sleeker and more intuitive menu
- Infinite preset slots
- Reworked Ring objects, these are now modular "pulses" and are highly configurable
- Seed-based randomization
- An undo-redo system
- An experimental "masking" mode for achieving perfect semi-transparency without use of a chroma-key

And now for a more detailed breakdown per section. A full changelog will be provided in the main release. Why not now? Because the prospect of writing such a document fills me with dread, and this post is going to be long enough without one!
[h2]Architectural stuff[/h2]
- The entire menu system has been rebuilt from the ground up. This menu supports different styling, which is even user-configurable, because the idea of having several hundred options to customize how your several hundred other options look was just too funny to pass up. Some pertinent information: holding E still temporarily hides the menu while inside the menu; clicking to the right of the menu in the blank area will spawn a note; [b]holding alt while interacting with a slider will allow finer adjustments to its value.[/b]

- Keysight now has an undo/redo system! Hooray! Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y ought to do useful things now. [b]This system has strong potential to cause strange behaviour and bugs.[/b] If you find any, please report them in the community hub.

- Preset slots are now infinite! Finally! There is also a "DonorPreset.sav" save file that specific presets can be saved to and loaded from within the new Preset Management tab. This is to allow users to share presets between each other a little easier. Save file is located in /AppData/Local/Keysight/Saved/Savegames

- The randomizer now operates based on seed values. This is actually way cooler than that sentence sounds, if you're a websocket-y kinda person.
[h2]Core settings[/h2]
- 3D camera controls (accessible by pressing F) have been rebuilt to behave more like a proper FPS. You can "flip" Keysight to act as though it's "wall-mounted" by setting Tilt and Local Roll to 0.
[h2]Note objects[/h2]
- Notes can now be forced into having the shape of white or black keys regardless of what key they actually are. So a C note can have the shape of a Db, but centred on C.

- Notes can now be manually stretched in the X and Z axis (which can be... goofy... but hey, you can do it)

- The underlying note-object architecture has been significantly tidied up, Keysight is now no longer switching between two different objects for "top down" and "bottom up" notes (don't even ask).
[h2]Note lights[/h2]
- No significant change
[h2]Keypresses[/h2]
- Keypresses now have alternate modes of fading out after the key has been released. The animation curve can also be controlled for alpha / horizontal / vertical fade-out modes.
[h2]Impact lights[/h2]
- The behaviour of the sustain pedal extending the lifetime of impact lights can now be disabled.
[h2]Pulses[/h2]
What are pulses? Pulses are the replacement to "rings". They can behave exactly the same as rings, or do so much more. They are modular, meaning that you can have as many of these stacked as you like (err, I am not responsible for ensuing lag if you spawn 50). Pulses take a texture as their shape source too, so once user-imported textures are back online these should be enormously powerful objects.
[h2]Particles[/h2]
- Particles slots are now infinite. Well, not [i]infinite[/i], since at some point your computer will explode.
[h2]Scene[/h2]
The new "Scene" tab contains non-dynamic scene element options. So, things like backdrop, piano materials, etc.

- Experimental masking mode. This button can be found under Component Visibilities, and is a very powerful button. It has a strong CPU overhead to it, but it switches Keysight to render two views simultaneously: a "normal" one and a "mask". It does this at an attempted Width x Height*2 resolution, but Unreal Engine will not make a window bigger than your desktop resolution, so some squishing might occur. This mode is intended to be used with the StreamFX plugin for OBS to take advantage of the Dynamic Mask filter, to apply the mask Keysight image to the normal Keysight image [b]to achieve semi-transparency without using a chroma-key, ensuring perfect edges and no loss of colour range.[/b]

- Backdrop can now behave like a "canvas" if Culling is disabled under Core Settings, and frame visibility is also disabled under Component Visibilities. This stretches the backdrop outwards by 10x, and is useful for non-standard Keysight implementations (such as 3D camera matched semi-transparent stuff so light spill is not contained to the edges of the frame)
[h2]Randomizer[/h2]
- Randomizer is now seed-based. This means if you give it a specific input string (alphanumeric characters only), it will always randomize to that exact preset. Please note that if you edit the randomizer settings, the same string may give different results in your own copy of Keysight versus someone else's, as you are changing the thresholds a random number is compared against to give a result (the random number will be the same though, so depending on what you edit, it might not be a huge change).
[h2]Hotkeys[/h2]
- Tons of new actions have been added as hotkey-triggerable events.
[h2]Graphics[/h2]
- No significant change
[h2]System[/h2]
- Lots of new options to control behaviour of the reworked menu!

- Websockets have been reworked. Full guide to follow soon(tm), but websockets can now send a password on connect, have many more actions available to be triggered. They can also send response messages back to the server, helping with chat integration on a stream and debugging.

- Menu styling menu. YEP. You have options for your options now. This isn't really intended to be used, because... why bother. But I needed a modular menu styling back-end for the menu rework, so in classic Keysight fashion it has been exposed to the user for modification if desired.

- Default material calibration. This allows you to set the internal "default" reference values Keysight uses in the randomizer, or when adding new presets.

[h1]Missing features in this beta[/h1]
This is not a complete build. It's going to take a while longer to get the final pieces in place for a public main-branch release, unfortunately. The following are absent:

- Basic menu mode
- Tooltips for most buttons
- Stats menu
- Most randomizer menu tabs
- Preset cycle/random looping modes
- Menu light mode (cue light mode joke)
- Individual preset reloading from file from within the menu

notes.title: Mac OS compatibility! Development roadmap!
notes.content:
[h1]Mac OS release is HERE![/h1]

For those who follow the development of Keysight very closely, you may have heard words along the lines of "I won't worry about figuring out Mac OS stuff for a long time yet". Well, err, about that: with some generous help from a Mac-based software developer, it happened a lot sooner than expected!

Not without sacrifice, however. Due to reliance on a Windows-only plugin, custom texture importing support has been stripped out of the Mac OS version [i]for now[/i]. This feature will be added back in soon to bring the Mac version up to full parity with Windows though! 

Additionally, the shadow casting option for impact lights has been disabled by default in the Mac OS release, due to shadows rendering incorrectly on Intel integrated graphics solutions. Keysight, in general, is a very graphics-intensive application, so please check out the Steam guide relating to performance optimization if you are struggling to maintain consistent framerates on a Mac device!

[h1]Roadmap[/h1]

While an announcement is being made, let's discuss the direction Keysight is heading in. Big old disclaimer: these plans are not set in stone, and there is no time-frame for this stuff! Keysight is developed on a hobbyist basis, and is considered a complete product to begin with. With that out of the way, here's what's coming:

[b]Huge menu overhaul.[/b] Ever wanted to change the settings of note indicators, so you click on the button labelled "note indicators", only to remember it's actually just under "settings"? That exactly situation happens to myself, and I literally built the damn thing. This kind of awful UX is not ok, and it's finally time to tackle it.

Furthermore, rebuilding all the menus from the ground up should allow for localization! Ensuring the technical accuracy of menu item localization will be very important, but I'm actively scouting out potential translators for Keysight already.

[b]Widgets![/b] What's a widget? Who knows, could be anything! Adding new features is hampered by the current menu backend. Rebuilding the menu should allow for little modules of functionality to be added much easier. Small extra Keysight features will be called "widgets", and these may include: a notes-per-second speedometer; pedalling indicator, etc. Widgets will be able to be placed freely in the scene, to fit into whatever your intended layout is!

[b]And then the much looser, "some day" stuff:[/b]
- Particle overhaul. We need to get those vector field particle paths into Keysight! Also... fireworks? Particle wind? So many options!
- Visual overlays. Things like refractive raindrop layers, underwater refraction effect, snowfall, leaves, that sort of thing!
- Different ways to visualize notes. Things like note indicators acting more like a "spectrum" audio visualization, spiking up and down based on note activity.

If you have any feature suggestions, don't forget to make a post in the community hub about it.

Happy Keysighting!

notes.title: Version 1.1.0 update!
notes.content:
[h2][b]Greetings![/b][/h2]

[i]It's been just over a week since the official public launch of Keysight, and high time the first of many updates goes live! Version 1.1.0 brings some fundamental features to both users who stream using Keysight, and users who create pre-recorded video content. Here's a breakdown of the new stuff![/i]

[h2]Midi channel preset mapping[/h2]

Under the Midi Hotkeys tab, you can now assign specific midi channels to specific preset slots. Using this, it is possible to visualize different instruments downmixed onto a single midi device that use different midi channels in a live context. More likely, however, is the use-case to [b]visualize the left and right hand individually[/b] by playing back an edited midi file where the hands are broadcast on different midi channels.

[h2]Websockets[/h2]

This is a big'un. Keysight now uses a SocketIO plugin for inbound and outbound web connectivity, allowing external triggering of any actions previously triggerable by midi-hotkey. On the inbound side of things, you can now bind an address and port to connect to, and then specify messages to listen for and execute commands. The use-case here is, of course, [b]chat controlled Keysight on your streams![/b] You can also specify a time to wait before executing any other websocket commands (which are sent to a queue), ensuring a user switching to a certain preset has a minimum time that Keysight stays in that preset.

For outbound messages, Keysight can now broadcast colour and note activity data to wherever you like using a standard JSON format. Using this, you could do all manner of crazy things like [b]IRL LED strips controlled by Keysight activity[/b] (which is itself controlled remotely!). When sending basic data, the colour slots from impact lights are blended through over time in a slow cycling manner and sent as a hex code, along with the total amount of note activity. Advanced data sends the hex code of all 88 impact light colours along with a 0-1 note activity value.

See documentation for the specifics!

[h2]Global core settings toggle[/h2]

A flag can now be set per-preset to use "global" core settings (height, speed, camera angle, key length, real-time mode). This alternate set of core data is stored in the System Prefs, and it enables a set-once workflow for your camera angle and scene set-up (rather than having to exhaustively, manually copy those variables across all 5 slots). This also allows [b]cleaner sharing of presets between users[/b] with different scene set-ups!

[h3]Full changelog notes[/h3]

--- Changes from 1.0.3a (first Steam release) to 1.1.0 ---

Fixed issue where cycling colour mode would always start at slot 1, not from ratcheted slot
Fixed issue where stats menu "begun tracking at" could display silly things like 16:5 as a time value
Fixed issue where closing main menu using the "close menu" button would not hide the cursor
Fixed issue with ramping values less than 1.00 appearing to make rings not alpha-fade correctly
Fixed issue where clearing a bound hotkey and immediately re-recording, and then mashing more than 8 notes to error-out the recording, would stop any hotkeys from being clear-able
Fixed issue with FMU failing to randomize note material
Fixed some minor misalignment issues with material picker / colour picker subheadings

Removed window resize ability on Keysight. For custom resolutions, dial it in manually under System

Changed Graphics menu resolution text fields to wipe themselves upon applying resolution
Changed colour colour picker slot names to use note names when relevant (series + 12 cycle number)
Changed code nativization settings. May see a ~0-5% performance hit depending on hardware and object pooling settings, but this allows greater flexibility in features moving forwards
Changed hotkey functionality to be scalable, apply to more actions, support multiple hotkeys for the same action, etc
Changed randomizer to pick a value between 13-39 for texture sizes when randomizing materials
Changed graphics option camera location/rotation to be text entry fields. No more endless buttons for no reason!
*Changed a ton of back-end stuff relating to note-on/off events and clearing of notes between realtime/non-realtime presets. Potential for strange behaviour, be on the lookout and report it if you see any!*

Added toggles to delay preset/randomization midi hotkey events by top-down time delay amount while in top-down mode
Added minimum note activation slider under Core while in advanced mode. Note-on events with lower than given velocity will not cause anything to happen
Added "open menu" button to preset bar if preset bar is set to "show" and menu is not open (for keyboard-less operation while preset bar is shown)
Added websocket connectivity for incoming commands (like switching presets and randomization), and outbound lighting data. See documentation
Added midi channel preset swapping under Midi Hotkeys. Incoming midi events can now be swapped to different presets based on channel data. Occurs "before" pedal switching
Added transposition functionality (to counter-transpose against instrument transposition). LIMITATION TO HOTKEYS: hotkeys will not function if transposition attempts to shift them outside the 21-108 midi control ID range
Added overdrive support to colour shift speed
Added randomizer toggle to bypass piano material randomization but keep backdrop randomizing
Added "use global settings" toggle. Uses set of speed/height/key length/time delay lock/camera settings saved in System Prefs instead of preset settings. Allows easier sharing and config of non-standard core setting presets

[h3]Save file update procedure for 1.0.3a to 1.1.0[/h3]

- Global core settings (eg height, speed, camera position) will be taken from Preset 1 and saved in System Prefs
- Use global core settings set to true for all presets
- Taken existing midi hotkeys and created identical hotkeys within new modular hotkey system
